text:
olivia: Drafting RFC for a combined change: smarter kernel selection + attention micro-ops + stricter KV cache eviction policy. Need reviewers and a short launch checklist.
kevin: :eyes: pinging infra and perf. what's the primary customer ask leading this?
tj: Customer ask = lower tail latency for multi-turn chat (HealthCo & RetailPilot). Also reduce token cost on steady-state.
maria: High-level acceptance criteria suggestion: 1) no >1% correctness regressions on our evals, 2) p95 latency non-worse for cold starts, 3) steady-state token cost reduced by >=8% on typical chat traces.
sara: Also add rollback criteria: any increase >5% in production error rate or >10% p95 latency bump on canary -> immediate rollback.
kevin: Technical scope: kernel selector to prefer fused kernels for GPT-like attention when seq_len<=512 and batch<=8; fallback to existing path otherwise. KV eviction: change from LRU to segmented-time-window evictor with TTL heuristics. Attention opt: add optional rotary fusion micro-op for small heads.
olivia: Proposed rollout: canary on Dedicated pool in us-west-2 for 24h with synthetic regen + 48h warm traffic. Then increase to 10% global for 72h with forced QA evals.
maria: Tests to add before canary: offline regression suite (50k prompts), loadtest harness with sequence shape distribution, and a mixed-quantization correctness pass.
tj: Edge cases to call out in RFC: 1) multi-GPU KV sharded requests (ensure eviction doesn't drop needed prefixes), 2) models with non-standard rotary position handling, 3) offload-to-CPU cases where fused kernels are slower.
kevin: Metrics we must publish: p50/p95/p99 tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, token-cost-per-1000, kv-hit-rate, model-correctness-score. Also expose a flag in telemetry to mark kernel variant used per request.
sara: Ops checklist: feature flag gated by model+pool, health check that verifies kernel selected matches expected for a couple sample models, automatic fallback on any unexpected kernel crash.
olivia: Acceptance criteria roundup from team: correctness regression <=1%, steady-state token cost -8%+, p95 at canary within +5% of baseline, and no crash/fallback frequency >0.1% in canary.
maria: Add an explicit security/compat note: no change to model weights or serialization; KV eviction only affects in-memory cache. Privacy OK.
kevin: Can we make the fused kernel opt-in per model in model-metadata? So we can skip for odd families.
tj: yes, plan: model metadata key `runtime.optimizer.kernels.fused: true|false` and `runtime.kv.evict.policy: segmented_ttl|lru`. Example config: ```json {"runtime.optimizer.kernels.fused": true, "runtime.kv.evict.policy": "segmented_ttl", "runtime.kv.ttl_ms": 300000} ```
sara: Who's signing off on rollout? Need Perf (kevin), ML infra (tj), QA (maria), Oncall (me). Also product to confirm launch messaging.
olivia: I'll loop in product after we lock acceptance criteria. Meeting to finalize RFC reviewers tomorrow 11am PT.
deploy-bot: Scheduled canary window: 2026-04-02T08:00Z -> 2026-04-03T08:00Z if gates pass.
kevin: Last note: record a short microbenchmark doc with seq shapes and kernel choices so support can explain regressions. Put it in eng-runtime/runs/ after canary.
maria: I'll draft the acceptance checklist in the RFC PR, include test names and exact eval set.
tj: I'll add a safety toggle that disables fused kernels per node at runtime.
olivia: perfect — assign owners in the PR: olivia (writer), kevin (perf), tj (infra), maria (QA), sara (oncall). Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
kevin: :shipit:
